functions.name: PyUnicode_IS_READY
functions.docs:
Fast check to determine whether an object is ready. Equivalent to:
PyUnicode_IS_COMPACT(op) || _PyUnicodeObject_CAST(op)->data.any

functions.name: PyUnicode_IS_ASCII
functions.docs:
Return true if the string contains only ASCII characters, or 0 if not. The
string may be compact (PyUnicode_IS_COMPACT_ASCII) or not, but must be
ready.

functions.name: PyUnicode_IS_COMPACT
functions.docs:
Return true if the string is compact or 0 if not.
No type checks or Ready calls are performed.

functions.name: PyUnicode_IS_COMPACT_ASCII
functions.docs:
Return true if the string is a compact ASCII string (use PyASCIIObject
structure), or 0 if not.  No type checks or Ready calls are performed.

functions.name: _PyUnicode_COMPACT_DATA
functions.docs: Return a void pointer to the raw unicode buffer.

functions.name: PyUnicode_GET_LENGTH
functions.docs:
Returns the length of the unicode string. The caller has to make sure that
the string has it's canonical representation set before calling
this function.  Call PyUnicode_(FAST_)Ready to ensure that.

functions.name: PyUnicode_WRITE
functions.docs:
Write into the canonical representation, this function does not do any sanity
checks and is intended for usage in loops.  The caller should cache the
kind and data pointers obtained from other function calls.
index is the index in the string (starts at 0) and value is the new
code point value which should be written to that location.

functions.name: PyUnicode_READ
functions.docs:
Read a code point from the string's canonical representation.  No checks
or ready calls are performed.

functions.name: PyUnicode_READ_CHAR
functions.docs:
PyUnicode_READ_CHAR() is less efficient than PyUnicode_READ() because it
calls PyUnicode_KIND() and might call it twice.  For single reads, use
PyUnicode_READ_CHAR, for multiple consecutive reads callers should
cache kind and use PyUnicode_READ instead.

functions.name: PyUnicode_MAX_CHAR_VALUE
functions.docs:
Return a maximum character value which is suitable for creating another
string based on op.  This is always an approximation but more efficient
than iterating over the string.
